title: An image is not a container

blocks.content: An image is a read-only stack of filesystem layers plus the metadata describing how to start it. A container is one running instance of that image with a thin writable layer on top.

items: One image can back a hundred containers
Writes land in the container's own layer, not the image
Delete the container and those writes go with it

blocks.title: The mental model
blocks.content: Image is to container what a class is to an instance, or a binary on disk is to a running process.
